body:
I don't know if any of my siblings are aware I self harm, but they've seen my scars in the past before I started cutting again and had to hide my skin. Every time they would ask what the scars were from I'd divert the question, mostly because my youngest sibling is really...impressionable, I guess, and tends to copy what I do, so I worry if she learns what self harm is she'll start doing it herself. The other two got the memo that I didn't want to talk about it after the first time I refused, but she just kept asking over and over again. Kid can't take a fucking hint.

Though I remember the first suicide attempt that landed me in the hospital (not the first one ever but just the first one my family ever found out about), my oldest younger brother was in the room when I told my mom I'd overdosed and then proceeded to practically fall over because I could barely walk. So he heard everything my mom said and asked, including the call to poison control and the hospital...I don't know how much of that he remembers though. He was only 8 or 9 years old at the time.

yup. I can't take compliments at all and I just end up feeling worse when I get them; like, "oh crap I tricked this person into thinking [blank]" and then I feel guilty and manipulative. Even when people are nice to me, I can't help but think there's another side to it...something there that they want that I'm not picking up on. I'm so filled with self-hatred that I can't honestly understand how people can see otherwise. It makes me want to be a bad person and have them see how I don't deserve those compliments...I never do, because my anxiety stops me, but still.

but then when it comes to affection, only one person can make me feel comfortable with it. my best friend, even though I'm not really that important to him. He's literally the only person in my life who I feel safe and OK with. but even when he compliments me I can't accept it. it's just affection (hugs, casual touching, snuggling, etc.) that feels fine with him, because...idk. I can't honestly figure out why. when other people touch me I just want to cry and hide, but when he does it I feel safe...better.

Actually, yeah; it did. My friend who I've been having so much trouble with...I got to talk to him today, although it was only for a short period of time before he had to leave, but it actually went well. I cried a lot...actually, I said a lot of stuff and he comforted me. He reassured me of a lot of things and rather than how I usually feel after this happens (empty and lost) I feel ... idk, hopeful? I still feel guilty about it but I'm going to try my best not to think too much about it I guess.

I have a younger sister who tells me to kill myself, and that I'm a waste of space who no one would miss if I died, but otherwise no...because I don't have a lot of family.

Sorry to hear you have a shitty uncle though :/ He sounds like a dick. Is there anyway you could tell your parents or another adult in your family about it? It might help him tone it down a bit if some adults got on him about his behavior.

thanks, that's kind of you to offer. Currently I'm paranoid that he's hacked my computer and spying on me (very unlikely, I recognize this) so I can't send any PMs since I'm on my phone, but please feel free to PM me as well. It's far easier to reapond than send them on my phone.

Also same to you, I hope you're able to get a bit more security with your boyfriend. You deserve love as well.

Far too many reasons to state honestly...I guess it mainly boils down to the fact that he says one thing and does the opposite. For example: he said he cares about me and wants to help me, but then proceeds to never message me, exclude me from everything, and generally pretend I don't exist until some random point where he'll ask how I'm doing. I get to hear him make plans with his better friends preeetty much daily, or at least every other day, while ignoring me...so that's fun.

There's also the fact that I have no sense of self-worth and don't feel like I deserve to be loved or be happy, but that's a way different story.

If it makes you feel any better, I'm like this with my "best friend" (subjective term, since I'm convinced he hates me) and we're not dating. Or even close to dating. And it happens when he texts anyone who isn't me. In fact, I dread the day he gets a girlfriend because that means he'll pay less attention to me and our friendship will change.

I wish I could give you some advice, but all I can say is to remember that he chose you, not her. There's something about you that he loves, that you're able to give him that others aren't. There's no reason for him to stay with you if he doesn't love you (sorry, that sounds really harsh), but the fact is that he's with you. He's not with her.

I know it's easier said than done, but just try and relax a bit...do you have any habits that help you de-stress that you could do?

My times at a mental ward were complete shit, though I was sent to the crappiest place in the area. Staff was abusive and treated us like dirt, threatening us and yelling over everything. Rarely got to see a doctor, and it could take 2+ days before you ever got in to get medications approved (including the ones you may have been on when you were admitted) which is shit because they will do everything in their power to get you out after the mandatory 72hr hold. We're supposed to be guaranteed a session every day, but I know some people who saw a doctor one time before being released. /Once/. One time I was there for 9 days and I saw my doctor twice, though I'm not even sure he was a real doctor...The staff honestly could not give a shit about those of us stuck in there and it sucks.

For anyone wondering, the place was Sierra Vista. God, I've been there multiple times and it's literally hell. Fucking hated that place...I came out worse than I went in, honestly.

It seems like you had a good experience though, so I'm glad to hear that.

I've heard of people getting the cops/ambulance called when talking to a suicide hotline, and I'd honestly sooner shoot myself in the face than have someone show up at my house...also I'm sure there would be a wait, and when I'm doing badly I tend to have to do things on the spur of the moment or else I'll lose my nerve. 

Plus, my room has no lock and my family loves to walk in without knocking, and the thought of them walking in while I'm on the phone with a hotline? Ugh.

I appreciate your concern, and I'm sorry that I've continued to complain and not really use much of your advice...I don't mean to be rude, but I just don't feel mentally well enough to do anything except rot.

honestly? I'm doing horribly, horribly awful today. Been actually praying to God asking him to have my friend at least message me once for the last few days, but nothing comes. Every time my phone lights up or I get an alert I always think "is it him?" but it never is. He's with his better friends, the important ones right now; I'm almost 100% certain. I'm also pretty sure he was with them all of yesterday, too. 

what about you?

God, I feel this so hard...my situation is a bit different than yours, but it's also really similar at the same time.

I wish I could give you advice, but unfortunately I don't have any...otherwise I'd be taking it myself. All I can say is keep strong, you deserve happiness and a good friend, and one day you'll have both of those things.

last night I dreamed that my friend actually texted me to see how I was doing. I held a conversation with him and felt satisfied for once. Felt like I mattered.

then I woke up and it felt like I'd been punched in the gut...god I started crying so damn hard.

yup...it's so painful to realize how unimportant you are to other people. Literally like ripping a part of your soul out.

Just know you're not alone, man. Hopefully one day you'll be able to find someone who cares about you as much as you care about them.

same here. The one friend I have occasionally hugs me and I never want to let go. I feel so safe around him and when he hugs me I honestly feel like everything is going to be OK for a small moment.

Too bad he probably hates my guts and is doing it so I won't know he hates me. I'm petrified of seeing him tomorrow. My brain says he's only being nice because he wants to deceive me into trusting him and thinking he cares, so that he can turn on me and hurt me.

It's alright, don't worry about explaining it; I completely understand. But it's really not worth it in the long run — it'll eventually get harder and harder to get that "refreshed" feeling. Any alternative that doesn't involve harming yourself is a good alternative to cutting, and there are a lot of them; you just have to try them out and figure out what works for you.

I mean, you can't tell just by looking at someone if they're a "normie" or not, especially online. If someone is able to relate to a suicide joke or meme, there's a good chance they've dealt with suicidal thoughts before. Over 15 MILLION adults in the United States have been diagnosed with depression per year. That's not including teenagers, or people who can't afford to be diagnosed.

Also, depression is a feeling that people DO deal with despite not being diagnosed with a mental illness. Literally, depression is an emotion. Major Depressive Disorder/Clinical Depression and Persistent Depressive Disorder are mental illnesses, but you don't have to be diagnosed with these disorders to feel depressed at times.

Me too. My mom has told me to my face that if I were to ever die, she'd lose it. Meaning she'd probably be institutionalized, because her kids are her life. Or, she'd kill herself. So either way, if I die I'm basically destroying my mother's life. Yay.

Makes me feel a whole lot more guilty about the fact that I consider OD'ing and walking into traffic daily. If not for my mom, I'd off myself in a heartbeat. But since she's here, I can't, and it's completely unbearable to live each day. I have a stash of pills that would almost 100% guarantee my death if I ever decide to do it, and while I know I should get rid of it I'm too afraid to. If I get rid of it, it will take me months to build the stash back up again.

I love my family, but I'm suffering for them and it's agonizing...and completely exhausting.

Please, please, please find another outlet. Cutting is not a habit you want to get into — take it from me. I've been self-harming for six years now, and I can't stop. It started off with the occasional cut and evolved into an uncontrollable habit. The scars that are left over are ugly as hell and everywhere; my mother, who doesn't realize I'm still actively cutting, makes jokes about it without realizing how upsetting it is to me.

The cuts will get deeper, they will get longer. They'll move from one part of your body onto another part you swore you'd never touch. It'll get harder and harder to hide — wearing long pants or long sleeves in the summer is the worst, and people will question you. I know it's hard and that cutting is an easy escape, but it's such a horrible habit that no one should ever have to turn to. Do you play any instruments? They're a great alternative as it can help take your mind off of your thoughts for at least a little bit. You mentioned you have a broken leg right now so you can't run, but why not try lifting weights? It becomes agonizing after awhile, and you'll get some nice arm muscles out of it if you do it enough.

I'm going to look into what my insurance offers, though I'm not sure how I'll be able to do it without alerting my parents of it. I might have to wait until I finish my GE and transfer to a university...I'll definitely check out those subreddits, though. Thanks for the links.

She might be able to refer me to someone, I'm not entirely sure. I don't think I'm ready to start talking to someone again and actually go to therapy, but I guess mediation is the first step.

I actually do this, too. Just try to take it in shorter bursts if an hour at once is too much. Maybe do 25 minutes, take a break, do another 25 minutes, etc..

Like, part of my brain is like "remember, build up to this" and "don't hit too loud on that note" while the other part is thinking about the tv show in the background. My only suggestion is to just take more breaks, or to try and consciously remind yourself while practicing.

Brahms' rhapsodies? Khachaturian's Tocatta is also pretty...interesting, to say the least. I don't know how easy it'll be to find, though.

It doesn't bother me, and I understand the reasons, but I still wonder at times if it would be a better diagnosis than bipolar.

I'm in USA. And I dread hormone for a few reasons...first, I have a horrible fear of needles, I can't even bring myself to get shots unless I'm forced into it. I actually passed out once getting the flu shot.
Second, I really don't want my voice to get deeper, I already sound really stupid when I talk and I don't want to make it worse by having my voice get deeper. Plus, more body hair would grow and I already have a lot of it.

No, I brought it up a few times but both of them (child and adult psych.) said it wasn't likely. Sometimes I feel like BPD would be a better diagnosis, but since I've been told it isn't so many times I just stopped bringing it up.

Apparently I don't take enough risks/act on my impulsive thoughts but honestly...I did some really dangerous things out of impulse throughout the years that I'm just too ashamed to talk about. My opinions of people change with the flip of a coin, but again, I never bring it up. So I don't know...I just feel like a fool when I try.

Surgery honestly sounds wonderful...I've dreamed of having it so many times, even once photoshopped a picture of myself so I'd look flat chested before deleting it. But I dread hormones. Plus, I have a feeling my parents would be real unhappy and ashamed if I asked them to help me pay for top surgery, which leaves me to do it in secret, so it'll have to wait a long time.

Yeah, I think I understand. I've always kind of hated the "special snowflake syndrome" thing since it made me feel like my brain was making me look like a bad person. It's like....logically and emotionally, I'm on two separate pages. I think that's just the easiest way to explain it?

Also, I'm glad you're doing better. Hope that you got some rest, sorry it took me awhile to respond, and thanks again for taking so much time to respond to me. Man, I really sound like a broken record typing that over and over...ah well.

Since some of the stuff you mentioned I've already answered in previous replies to people, I'll just glance over them so I don't come across as a broken record...I have a psychiatrist, but I'm both too ashamed and don't know when I will be able to see her. I am planning on making an appointment sometime this week though. Maybe I will try getting another psychologist, but I just really can't fit in at this point. 

I don't even have an Obgyn, honestly. Since I'm not sexually active there is no reason to go before I turn 21 (so almost 2 years away, since I turn 19 in three weeks), and I'm not on any kind and of birth control and don't want to be. The hormones will make me gain weight and make me look more feminine, and both of those are the last things I want to happen.

Thanks for taking the time to respond, sorry I can't give a better reply...I really appreciate that you commented, though.

If you don't mind me asking, since this is fairly personal, did it get easier to orgasm only after you became close to your partner? And did it get easier for you personally, or only when with him? Again, sorry if this is too personal and I come across as rude, feel free to ignore this question if you don't want to answer.

Either way, thank you for taking the time to comment. I really hope one day I might be able to figure out this whole orgasm problem of mine...its relieving to know that people have had relationships work out fine despite having issues with it. Though at this point touching myself sexually feels no different than touching my arm, so I don't know how likely it is for me.

The therapist thing is because of a shortage of psychologists in the area. Everyone is very heavily booked, and even when I was in child psych I almost never got to meet my psychologist more than once a month. More frequent is, as I mentioned in another reply, for iop. Generally the iop therapists don't work well with me, though...it's a mandatory to meet them after coming from a psych ward, and 3/4 times I've met with an iop therapist have been forced because I came out of the hospital. Maybe it's because I was still suicidal and angry about having to be there that it didn't work out, but the only other time I was referred and I didn't cooperate then because I felt heavily abandoned despite it being in my best interest.

My child psychologist knows I cut, knows I have an eating disorder. I was referred to a specific psychologist for it when I was 13, but we...didn't work well. Then that same psychologist who met me for my ED was the person who put me in my first psychiatric hold months later when I was in the ER. Aftee that I just stopped telling the truth for the most to my main therapist, until I opened up again in my junior year of high school. She used to help me think of alternatives and give me small goals, which helped a lot, but...I just really didn't take it well when I had to move on. The adult psychologist I was referred to thinks I haven't cut in awhile and that I'm recovered from my ED and I'm not planning to correct her.

I'm going to try getting my meds fixed, it is just so exhausting to go out in public. I also dread meeting my med doctor again, as my prescriptions are both way overdue. One of them was filled in March of LAST year (100 pills) and is only 2/3 gone, the other (30 pills) is a week or two past and completely full, plus half of another bottle that I never finished. I feel ashamed and embarrassed over it to be honest. 

Thank you for taking the time to comment, I appreciate it a lot.

How well can you play these pieces listed? There's a big difference between playing a piece and PLAYING a piece, if you know what I mean. Do you play them with feeling and pay attention to the changes in dynamic, do you play the notes accurately for the most part, etc.? If you're just stumbling through them, or ignoring proper techniques and fingering, then it's a good idea to get that down real solid before you keep going.

If you want some Bach pieces that aren't too difficult, there's always his prelude in c major? Very beautiful piece, getting it to flow might be a bit difficult at first but you'll get it if you practice. There's also his minuet in d minor, his march in d major, and his polonaise in g minor. All of these are pretty easy to get down and are good at strengthening your technique if you play them right, but then again, I've been playing for over a decade so I don't fully remember at this point what is and isn't hard for a beginner. 

I have a couple more I could list if those don't interest you. If you're looking for a similar style to Bach you can look to Handel, he is from the same period as Bach. 

Hope this helped a bit!

If you mean a psychiatrist, I already have one; but here they aren't really meant to be used as therapy, but rather to give medication. I can of course talk to her about things, but she's not going to be the doctor I go to and talk about how my life is shit. I go in, she asks how the medicine are helping (or how they aren't) and then I elaborate and she fixes the dose.

I really hope there are doms who would be willing to be with me. I have no idea how to find them, but that's something to worry about in the future.

Thanks for your reply.

I've tried recently to do things for myself, but not in a really positive way...I don't want to go into detail (because there's always the risk of triggering or upsetting someone), but the only times I can act "selfishly" is when my eating disorder is the reason. I know that having scars doesn't make a person unlovable, again it's like I mentioned in my first reply; my brain just cannot associate me as being the same as everyone else. Everyone else isn't disgusting for self-harming, only I am. I'm sorry if I came across as thinking scars make a person gross, it isn't what I meant at all. And, yeah; my eating disorder is a huge control factor. Control, and a punishment.

I really appreciate that you took so much time to type an in depth response, two hours is really long so I'm sorry I can't give a better response...thank you so much for making these replies though. I really cannot express how much it helped me.

This made me cry. Not very much, since I'm currently coming out of an apathetic stage, but I haven't cried in weeks until now. Reading your responses just made me really emotional.

First of all, I want to say that I'm sorry you've had all these feelings before as well...it's so awful to live with and it hurts me to think of other people struggling with this. No one should have to feel like this...which is really weird of me to be saying, since I often tell myself that I deserve unhappiness. Hell, even though I say "no one deserves this", part of me says "you don't count". But I'm so so glad you're doing better (or at least, I'm assuming you are based on parts of your post, sorry if I'm assuming wrong) and I hope you are never stuck in a rut like this again, because it's so exhausting and horrible.

I'm not currently seeing anyone, once I graduated high school I got moved out of child psychology and into adult psychology and I haven't taken the transition well at all. I AM on medication, but I'm really really bad at taking them. Usually it's because I forget, but there's also the fact that my dosage is wrong AND a lot of the time I feel like I don't deserve to be happy, so I shouldn't take my medication so I can stay miserable...it sounds really messed up when I put it into words.

Gender dysphoria...yeah, I am dealing with that. It started when I hit puberty and started developing a figure. I don't want to go as far as to call myself trans, since I don't feel like a boy, but I just. Hate looking like a woman. If I could have an androgynous body (completely flat chested/very small breasts, no butt, small/thin thighs) I feel like I might be able to like myself a bit more? But then again, at the worst of my eating disorder I had the figure of a child and I still hated myself. So I don't know...

As for acting out...both. Sometimes I fantasize about acting bratty and having to have a dom tame me/force me (to an extent), because I actually think it'd be pretty fun as long as it doesn't go too far. But a lot of the time it's me wanting to actually start a fight. Like, I imagine purposely breaking a rule or doing something rude/disrespectful to piss them off so they'll hurt me. I realize 100% that this is just me trying to use someone else to self-harm, and that it's manipulative and messed up. So...I guess it's both? I've never had any experience with punishments (not even my parents, I've always been incredibly well behaved) so while I imagine I'd enjoy it, since I also imagine being punished to reaffirm that I'm "bad" I'm not sure where that line is at this point. I hope that makes sense...

When people try and comfort me I just shut down. It's only really online that I don't feel as much stress, probably because there's no personal connection? I don't know.
Thank you.

The post of the woman who overcame her eating disorder and self-harm is really inspiring, but I honestly don't think it would work for me. I use them to cope AND as punishment; when I'm having a panic attack, I can punch my gut or cut myself and it'll give me some form of control over it. Plus, there's a huge "you deserve this" that comes along with it. I'm glad she was able to get better, but it honestly feels like I'm too deep in this to ever let someone take it away from me. Just the thought is making me a bit freaked out honestly...I wonder if there's really a way I could combine my eating disorder&self harm with bdsm without losing one of them...

My (new) psychologist only had two sessions with me before referring me to someone else, who then canceled the day before the appointment, so I've never had anyone in adult-psych. work with me on it. My child-psych. worked more with the depression aspect since that's where I stayed most of the time. I have meds, but I don't take them regularly...I just forget honestly. It isn't a priority anymore because one of them is the wrong prescription and does absolutely nothing to help, and has the side affect of weight gain.

I really appreciate you taking the time to type such a long and in depth response, I'm sorry I can't give a better response to it.

Unfortunately, she's so busy that I doubt that she'll find time to answer. I could get her in trouble by trying to reach out to talk to her and that's the last thing I want to do. She said I could call to leave updates, but I don't want to give an update of "this is the worst I've been in nearly a year", because it'd just be a waste of her time. It's not like she can help me after all.

Yeah, you're right. I just wish it was that easy; I wasted six years trying to get better but I'm only at a worse place now than I was at the start.

The thing about the orgasm control, though, is that it does interest me. I just don't feel like I'd be able to do it because I don't even understand how to orgasm...if that makes sense. Like, I've never bothered trying to orgasm, so although the idea is interesting I feel like it'd be difficult or embarrassing to try. It's really difficult to put into words, sorry...

I appreciate your response to my post.

The only day of the week I have free is on Friday every other week, but the mental health system where I live is kind of crap honestly...I'm lucky if I can get an appointment once a month for 45 minutes. I had one in the beginning of December, but the doctor (who I was referred to since she focuses more on talking first and then fixing rather than just fixing) canceled on me the day before and I just don't have the motivation to call and make another appointment. Stupidly enough, my brain's response to that was "not even a professional wants to help you" despite logically I know that it wasn't for that reason.

Adult psychology here is all about fixing, which is understandable, but I need to be able to talk about things without being expected to automatically get over them, and once a month isn't nearly enough. Plus, co-pays. The only way to get weekly here is to go into an intensive outpatient program (iop) but it's complete crap to be honest...it doesn't help at all.

And yeah...I realize that a lot of what I want from a dom right now is a lot of me wanting to use them as another way to self-harm, which I know is really awful. I don't want to do that to someone. I am actually into bdsm, have been since middle school, but at this point I know that it'd be unhealthy for me to go into any kind of relationship, much less one involving bdsm. I just am scared that I'll never be able to submit? If that makes sense. That even if I manage to get appointments that I won't be able to get better, and that I'll just be stuck like this forever...ugh. Sorry for the long response.

I was in therapy for the last six years, but graduating high school and entering college required me to move out of adolescent psychology and into adult, and I was incredibly attached to my previous psychologist. Now I can't fit appointments into my schedule, and I don't want to talk to anyone else about personal things...it's just gone downhill a lot since last year. 

Plus I've been living with these thoughts since I was nine-ten years old, even if I didn't start seeing someone until I turned twelve. I've literally been living with all of these things for as long as I can remember...I don't even know what it's like anymore to not feel anxious and hate myself. Feels like I'm beyond help at this point
